newsitem.title: UK: Elf says it not rejected for Iraqi oil deal.
newsitem.headline: Elf says it not rejected for Iraqi oil deal.

text.p: Elf Aquitaine denied on Wednesday that it had been rejected by the United Nations in an attempt to buy Iraqi crude oil.
An Elf spokesman said the company had not signed a contract yet to lift Iraqi oil under a U.N. limited sale plan but is interested in buying Iraqi oil.
"We have always said we are interested in buying Iraqi oil but to say Elf was rejected by the United Nations is wrong. We have not submitted a contract," the spokesman said.
On Tuesday, U.N. sources said overseers charged with reviewing all oil contracts under the Iraqi oil-for-food plan rejected a deal between Elf and Iraq.
They said the contract was rejected because the Iraqi state oil and marketing organization (SOMO) wrongly posted the contract directly to the U.N.
Industry sources expect Elf and fellow French oil company Total to be among the first to sign contracts with Iraq now that the much-postponed deal has been approved.
The first contract to be submitted for overseer perusal was between SOMO and Turkish company Tupras for 75,000 barrels per day over six months.
